This weekend, my team ( Aryan Jain , Ryan Ding ) and I built Train of Thought, a tool to run two LLM agents in parallel and implement a type of chain of thought thinking! By using two agents to break down a prompt, generate a chain of thoughts, and verifying subproblem outputs, we saw accuracy and safety improvements over a one-shot approach. This was inspired by OpenAI 's recent o1 model as well as research in the field of multi-agent LLMs. Currently, the project uses two instances of Google 's Gemini Flash 1.5 model, but this approach can be generalized to any number and type of models. Potential Applications: - Safety: Ensure agents are obeying safety policies by using each agent to moderate the other. - Accuracy: Improve accuracy of the overall system by breaking down prompts and ensuring each subproblem is solved correctly. - Backtracking: Agents backtrack if incorrect output is seen at any stage. - Multi-Agent Learning: One agent can learn from another agent by using it to provide overall reasoning about a prompt. In the future, this system can use a collection of models, each with their own specialties. Overall, working on this project was a blast and a great learning opportunity for all of us. If your interested in learning more about the project please reach out! I would love to chat. ...more ...more

Thank you to our friends at Nasdaq for a fantastic morning ringing the opening bell. Physical AI is here today, and Kodiak is in the driver’s seat!

As Kodiak approaches its one-year anniversary as a public company, I have the honor of celebrating by ringing the opening Nasdaq bell on Wednesday morning! A year ago, I outlined a vision for transforming the way freight moves through Physical AI. Today, that is no longer a mere vision, but a reality. Physical AI is being commercialized and delivering real-world impact. Kodiak already has its driverless technology deployed in 35 trucks that operate with no one in the cab, the largest fleet of its kind in the world -- and up from five trucks one year ago. A huge thank you to the incredible Kodiak team, our amazing partners, and all the other stakeholders who have executed and made this possible. We’re just getting started. Please take a moment and celebrate our one-year milestone with us Wednesday morning starting at 9:15 a.m. ET with the market open at 9:30. Link in the comments to watch the bell-ringing live! #PhysicalAI $KDK

Built for the challenges of industrial operations. The Kodiak Driver is operating driverless across the Permian Basin, adapting to unstructured roads, dynamic routes, and changing load configurations. From single trailers to doubles and triples, it’s designed for environments where flexibility is a requirement, not an exception.

This summer, we welcomed interns across several of our offices, where they supported teams throughout the firm while gaining meaningful, hands-on experience in a collaborative environment. To complement their work, interns participated in a professional development program that included: • Corporate Etiquette Workshop • Internship Breakfast • Mid-Summer Lunch • Analyst Q&A Series Featuring Nine Analysts Discussing the Transition from University to Corporate Life • Resume Workshop • Networking Workshop • A City Harvest Volunteer Event Supporting the Local Community Throughout the summer, interns also had the opportunity to connect with colleagues through office-specific activities, including team outings to a Colorado Rockies game and a NYC summer happy hour, further strengthening relationships across the firm. We are grateful to our interns for their contributions and to the colleagues who invested their time in mentoring, sharing their experiences, and helping create a rewarding internship experience. Over the coming weeks, we’ll be sharing a series of videos featuring several of our interns as they reflect on their internship experience and the insights they gained along the way. Shayegan Omidshafiei , FieldAI President and Chief Scientist, gave the keynote “Autonomy in the Wild” at AUTONOMOUS: The Future of Robotics & Physical AI in San Francisco. The premise: what does it take for a robot to arrive at a site it has never seen, with no prior map, no GPS, and no site-specific training—and get to work? FieldAI robots do exactly that across hundreds of deployments in construction, energy, and other complex industrial environments, where conditions are constantly changing and robots must operate safely around people, equipment, and incomplete information. Full keynote linked here: https://lnkd.in/g-qyy7EE

I have always held strong conviction in Kodiak ’s leadership position. It is, of course, nice to see it confirmed in independent metrics like The Road to Autonomy® 's Autonomous Truck Index. Kodiak’s technology is deployed in 35 driverless trucks, as of June 30, the largest customer owned-and-operated fleet of semis in the world.

July was my last month at Kodiak . The past 8 years have been exciting and incredibly rewarding. I started about 5 weeks after the company was founded with nothing but a laptop and a rack full of snacks, and led the company as CTO to the first full commercial launch of a driverless trucking fleet - 24/7 operations, owned and operated by the customer - in 2024, followed by Kodiak’s public listing on NASDAQ in 2025. As of June 2026, Kodiak had 35 driverless trucks deployed at the customer’s site, having operated 40,000+ cumulative paid hours without anyone in the cabin. The latest software release further increased efficiency by 30%, all in a harsh environment with oncoming, third-party traffic. And it also isn’t just the one vehicle, because not all customers want the same: we built several driverless platforms, from big semis to offroad vehicles, that could operate safely in their respective environments. Most recently, the team delivered the first driverless daycab that I know of, on yet another new OEM base platform and with a new Gen7 generation of autonomy hardware. This isn’t just technology, it’s a full product that is actually useful to customers - and that product focus has been in Kodiak’s DNA from day one. Behind the scenes, the reality of Physical AI is amazingly complex: It took designing a system from the ground up that could meet the rigor of a full safety assessment to launch in 2024 and repeatedly after; finding and hiring hundreds of excellent people to refine and execute the plan; coordinating OEMs, suppliers, contract manufacturers, and partners around the world and earning their trust over years; real-world testing in both hot and icy conditions from the Permian to Michigan, and many interstates between; testing in simulated environments that reflect all of those conditions with well understood fidelity; and aligning the software, hardware, and systems engineering so we could operate safely and efficiently at the same time. I was part of it at every step, leading, helping, and motivating; but the real credit goes to the team at Kodiak who did the hard work on the ground and made it happen. I keep being impressed by what this team is able to do, often on tight timelines and tighter budgets. I’ve seen first hand how listening well, sharing insights, and helping others grow will exponentially increase the impact of an organization. Thank you for giving me the opportunity and trust to lead you through the ups and downs every startup goes through on the way to success. It’s been an incredible experience! Now it’s time to make space for the next generation of leaders at Kodiak. I've been enjoying time with family, both here in the US and in Austria, and reconnecting with people I haven't had a chance to talk to for way too long. If you're around, let's chat - I'd love to catch up.
